doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Why blues is dominated by white players, and a joke
summary: Rowe and Johnstone discuss white players in the blues, black musicians moving beyond the image, and a joke about selling one's soul to Santa.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: If you look at the blues scene especially, it seems to be mostly dominated by white players.
It’s like obligatory to wear a hat. You can’t play the blues without a hat.
Do you have an idea of why black musicians don’t pursue the blues? I mean it’s not like it’s a great way to make a living I suppose, but I think there’s something beyond that.

Yeah, I think there’s some major social issues, that the black musicians want to move beyond that image. I heard a great joke. Remember Robert Johnson, the legendary guitar player who went down to the crossroads at midnight and sold his soul to Satan?
Well there was a dyslexic blues player who decided that he was going to do the same thing. So he went down to the crossroads at midnight and sold his soul to Santa.
And he probably had better luck. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-
